food_database: Miłek et al. 2023, Figure 4/results, common barberry fruit
food_database_record_id: Figure 4; textual result identifies B. vulgaris (L) and B. vulgaris (S), respectively
synonym_verification_status: Exact berberine analyte named; Stage B CID/InChIKey copied from registered identity audit
mapping_review_rationale: Manual exact target mapping: source reports berberine fruit content and HPTLC band matches an authentic berberine sulfate standard by Rf; Stage B CID/full InChIKey independently checked against PubChem. Sulfate-standard mass-expression and co-migrating alkaloid uncertainty are explicitly retained; no Stage B edits.
moisture_basis: Sample was freeze-dried (wild fruit) or purchased dried (market sample); authors do not explicitly state a moisture correction. Do not convert to fresh-weight basis.
analytical_method: HPTLC on silica gel 60 F254; UV 366 nm fluorescence densitometry; identity by matching Rf (0.20) to 99% berberine sulfate standard; calibration 0.5–2 µg per band, R²=0.9906
extraction_method: 5 g milled lyophilized fruit extracted with 25 mL 70% ethanol in two 20-minute ultrasonic cycles at ≤50°C; filtered
sample_size: One field-derived wild fruit sample and one commercially purchased dried-fruit sample; three analytical replicates per sample; no independent biological replicate series reported
source_title: The analysis of berberine content in the fruits of various species of barberry (Berberis sp.) by high performance thin-layer chromatography (HPTLC)
database_reference: Miłek et al. 2023, Postępy Fitoterapii 24(1):3–8; Materials and Methods; Results; Figure 4
extraction_notes: Reported mean 5.46 mg/100 g lyophilized/dried fruit, arithmetically converted to 54.6 mg/kg on the same basis. Source does not give a numeric SD in the searchable text; Figure 4 depicts mean ± SD from triplicate analytical measurements. No SD value inferred. Promoted as the source-author-reported berberine fruit estimate (mg/100 g); HPTLC quantitation used 99% berberine sulfate standard. No cation/salt conversion was invented.
uncertainty_notes: HPTLC identity is based on matching retention factor to berberine sulfate standard; authors observe an additional yellow alkaloid band. Confirm whether mass concentration is berberine cation or berberine-sulfate equivalent. No fresh-weight conversion. Commercial dried fruit came from an herbal-products retailer, so ordinary food-market provenance needs review. Analytical triplicates are not independent biological samples. Candidate only; Stage B checksum gate remains active. Berberine-sulfate calibration mass-expression is not explicitly resolved, so retain source-reported concentration as method-specific estimate; an additional yellow alkaloid band was observed. Commercial dried sample source was an herbal-products retailer; wild sample is a single field collection. Three analytical replicates are not independent biological replicates.
